title: Cats Cats Cats – A decentralized multiplayer voxel game where every animal is a cat hybrid
author: SamAutomaton
selftext:
**Play free in your browser (no sign-up):** [https://catscatscats.net/play](https://catscatscats.net/play)

**Discord:** [https://discord.gg/GM8exUFP](https://discord.gg/GM8exUFP)

I have been writing C++ and building games for 25 years, long before AI existed. Over the past 3 months I have been building **Cats Cats Cats**, a cross-platform (Web, Desktop, and Android, with the Web build public right now) decentralized multiplayer voxel sandbox in custom C++, WebAssembly, and WebGPU where every animal is a cat hybrid (Cat-Horses, Cat-Pigs, Cat-Chickens, all of it).

Everyone plays together in one shared world with a permanent Home World and outer wilds that regenerate over time, with zero accounts and zero player tracking.

**How I use AI in my workflow:**   
I design and architect the engine, networking, and gameplay systems myself, and use **Claude and Gemini** to write C++ and WebGPU implementation code, shaders, and boilerplate much faster than I could type it alone. I also used AI to generate the music tracks so I could focus my time on engine performance and gameplay instead of audio production. Knowing C++ inside and out makes it easy to review everything they output, catch bad patterns immediately, and keep the codebase clean while shipping at a fraction of the usual solo-dev timeline.

UI art is still placeholder, so ignore the temporary menus. Since there is zero telemetry in the game, I only know what happens if you tell me.   
  
If you give it a spin, I'd love to know:   
**Did you make it to the gnome village and find the relic block?**

*(There's also an in-game Feedback button inside your inventory.)*
